newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians say U.S. veto hinders peace process.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians say U.S. veto hinders peace process.

text.p: Palestinian officials said on Saturday that Middle East peace efforts would be hindered by the United States veto of a U.N. resolution calling on Israel to drop plans for a new Jewish neighbourhood in mostly Arab East Jerusalem.

The Security Council vote late on Friday was 14 in favour, with only the U.S. voting against. As one of the council's five permanent members, its vote killed the resolution, drafted by Britain, France, Portugal and Sweden.
"The American decision will negatively affect the progress in the peace process," said Nabil Abu Rdaineh, President Yasser Arafat's adviser.

The veto followed a council debate in which virtually all the nearly 50 speakers condemned Israel's plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews at a site called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.

"We feel very sorry over the American decision to use its veto power against the decision which was about to be taken by the Security Council against the Israeli decision to build at Abu Ghneim," Rdaineh said.
Israel regards the entire city of Jerusalem as its capital while the Palestinians see East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.

U.S. ambassador Bill Richardson criticised the Israeli action, both during the debate and after casting his veto, saying it undermined trust and confidence so badly needed in the Middle East peace process.
But he said the council was... "not an appropriate forum for debating the issues now under negotiation between the parties."
Israel welcomed the U.S. veto but slammed the European states that drafted the resolution, calling them "one-sided".

"We view gravely the European initiative which is unbalanced and one-sided and contrary to the position of the other members of the Security Council, said Freddy Eytan, an adviser to Foreign Minister David Levy.

The Palestinian Liberation Organisation's United Nations observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, speaking after the veto, said: "In view of the failure of the council to fulfil its obligations, we would request from the members of the United Nations to agree to a meeting of the General Assembly in an emergency session."
There is no veto in the 185-member Assembly, whose decisions are not binding.
